findings.title: Cancellation persistence failure skips termination and disables timeout fallback
findings.precondition: A command is running and Cancel is called with the current epoch; persist returns an ordinary file-write/replace error.
findings.derivation: Cancel sets Cancelled=true before persist. On persistence failure it returns before killJob. The polling timeout branch requires !Cancelled, so subsequent deadline/timeout expiry cannot trigger that branch.
findings.impact: The current command can continue until natural exit despite cancellation intent and a cleared pending queue. This does not claim any experimentally observed Windows API outcome.
findings.expected_followup: Keep cancellation intent distinct from termination attempts; preserve the persistence error while ensuring cancellation still attempts termination. Add a journal-failure regression.

findings.title: A later successful command overwrites an earlier protocol failure
findings.input_description: Two queued commands: first exits 0 with JSONL {"type":"turn.failed"}; second exits 0 with JSONL {"type":"turn.completed"}.
findings.derivation: The first Parse result records request_failed, but the loop only stops for nonzero exit or cancellation. The next command overwrites Journal.Protocol. Its successful completion leaves only the successful protocol summary and a final SETTLED lifecycle state.
findings.impact: The aggregate outcome loses the earlier protocol failure and the next queued command starts. No direct product ACCEPTED transition was observed or claimed.
findings.expected_followup: Retain per-command protocol results and define failure-aware queue progression and aggregate outcome. Add a first-fails/second-succeeds regression.

bounded_observations: Within one Parse call, an accumulated failure is not cleared by a later duplicate turn.completed event.
